children: RentoMojo’s Rs 1,255.6 crore IPO delivered big exits via OFS. Accel sold shares for Rs 317 crore; Chiratae and GMO fully exited. Co-founder Geetansh Bamania sold Rs 34.31 crore worth, retaining a 13.37 per cent stake

Furniture and appliance rental startup RentoMojo’s IPO has delivered sizeable returns for its early backers through its offer-for-sale component, ahead of the startup’s stock market debut, according to a media report.

Cofounder Geetansh Bamania pocketed Rs 34.31 crore by selling 8.49 lakh shares at the issue price of Rs 404 apiece. Before the bidding process began, Bamania said he had initially planned to sell nearly 20 lakh shares through the offer-for-sale but later reduced the size of the sale as he turned more bullish on the company and its future prospects. Following the IPO, Bamania retains a 13.37 per cent stake in RentoMojo, comprising 1.40 crore shares valued at Rs 567.56 crore at the issue price.

Institutional investors also clocked sizeable gains from the offer-for-sale. Accel India, RentoMojo’s largest institutional shareholder, sold 78.47 lakh shares for around Rs 317 crore, translating into a gross return multiple of 8.6 times on the shares sold based on the investor’s weighted average acquisition cost. Accel retains around 1.34 crore shares in RentoMojo, valued at approximately Rs 541 crore at Rs 404 apiece.

Madison India pocketed Rs 96.9 crore by selling 23.99 lakh shares, clocking a gross return of 7.2 times. It retains 43.39 lakh shares valued at approximately Rs 175 crore. Edelweiss Discovery Fund and ValueQuest clocked gross returns of around 5.4 times each on the shares sold.

For IDG Ventures India Fund III LLC, which is managed by Chiratae Ventures, the IPO marked a complete exit from RentoMojo. The investor sold its entire holding of 28.03 lakh shares for Rs 113.3 crore, representing a gross return of around 5 times. Chiratae Trust and Pratithi Investment Trust partially cashed out their holdings. Chiratae sold 20 lakh shares for around Rs 80.9 crore, clocking a gross return of 4.9 times. It retains 2.52 lakh shares valued at approximately Rs 10 crore.

GMO Payment Gateway Inc sold 15.13 lakh shares for Rs 61.1 crore, while GMO GFF Ltd Partnership sold 8.42 lakh shares for around Rs 34 crore. Both investors exited RentoMojo completely, clocking gross returns of 4.3 times and 4.2 times, respectively. Venture Catalysts++, which also made a complete exit, sold 76,000 shares for approximately Rs 3.1 crore, representing a gross return of 5 times.

Some of the biggest return multiples from RentoMojo’s IPO accrued to its individual investors. Nazara Technologies founder Nitish Mittersain pocketed around Rs 6 crore by selling 1.48 lakh shares. Based on his weighted average acquisition cost, the transaction translated into a gross return of 152.45 times. Mittersain retains 78,460 shares valued at approximately Rs 3.17 crore.

Rajeev Chitrabhanu HUF clocked an even higher return. It pocketed Rs 12.4 crore by selling 3.07 lakh shares, translating into a gross return multiple of 265.97 times. The HUF retains 30.73 lakh shares worth approximately Rs 124.2 crore.

Renaud Laplanche, cofounder and CEO of US-based fintech company Upgrade, completely exited RentoMojo through the IPO. He sold 7.55 lakh shares for around Rs 30.5 crore, generating a gross return of 5.38 times.

RentoMojo’s Rs 1,255.6 crore IPO comprised a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 150 crore and an offer-for-sale of up to 2.74 crore shares worth Rs 1,105.6 crore. The startup had reduced the offer-for-sale component from the 2.84 crore shares proposed in its draft red herring prospectus. The issue received bids for 158.68 crore shares against 2.18 crore shares on offer, taking the overall subscription to 72.88 times at the end of the three-day bidding period.

Ahead of the public issue, RentoMojo raised Rs 376.1 crore from 41 anchor investors by allotting 93.1 lakh shares at Rs 404 apiece. Founded in 2014 by Geetansh Bamania and Ajay Nain, RentoMojo operates a subscription-based rental platform for furniture, appliances and other home essentials. As of March 2026, it had 8.5 lakh live items across furniture and appliances and 2.5 lakh live subscribers.

The company’s operating revenue grew 45.5 per cent to Rs 387 crore in FY26 from Rs 266 crore in FY25. Its profit after tax jumped nearly 142 per cent year-on-year to Rs 104.3 crore, although it included a Rs 36.6 crore tax credit. Meanwhile, EBITDA rose 38 per cent year-on-year to Rs 163.5 crore, with the margin narrowing to 41.5 per cent from 43.6 per cent. RentoMojo generated around Rs 170 crore in operating cash flow during FY26, while incremental capex stood at about Rs 175 crore as it expanded its rental inventory.
